description: [S7.8, kind `method`] The app presents at the frame code's Window::refreshFull drop (tick's TkBase::call), but the modal screens that issue their drawing through their own module (credits_gx in commands_screens.inc, routing.cpp MapDraw, saveload.cpp's browser, peer_optional) hand Window::refreshFull to gfx_drop directly, so their back buffer reaches the app's window at the next modal pump ('m'), not at their refreshFull as in the original (refreshFull -> Window::refreshRect 0x00480c20 -> drawTooltip 0x0047cdb0 -> Display::present at 0x0047cfba). Measured: sandbox_basic 3 'm' presents, course_season_6y 3; how many passes of those screens draw between their refreshFull and their pump was not counted.
path to resolution: Route those modules' Window::refreshFull calls through one helper that also calls the live run's present_point (tk::cur_io().live), a change in the 3.7b / 38 modules' files

description: [S7.8, kind `scope`] The original also presents outside Window::refreshFull: uiPointerMove 0x004959b0 (the jgld Listener's slot 5, WM_MOUSEMOVE) runs compositeScreen 0x0047fab0 or drawCursor 0x0047d130, Tooltip::show 0x00480220 / hide 0x00480360 and redrawRegion 0x00495770 (slot 1, WM_PAINT) each end in drawTooltip's Display::present of a dirty rect, after drawing the cursor / tooltip into the back buffer. The port draws neither the software cursor nor tooltips (no gfx body for drawCursor / drawTooltip), so the app shows nothing new on a mouse move in game. Not measured whether the in-game cursor of the original is drawCursor's sprite or the system cursor.
path to resolution: A gfx body family for drawCursor / drawTooltip (S2 / S3), then a present_point at those drops

description: [S7.8, kind `measure`] Before S7.8 the live core held every frame record (T + 203 sim hashes, 1,628 B per frame) and every recorder event in memory until the session ended; over course_season_6y on the app's live path (51,092 frames) private bytes grew from 199,475,200 at frame 0 to 365,592,576 at the end (3.3 KB per frame). With RecordStreams (framehash.bin per record, trace.trace spilled every 4,096 events) private bytes are 230,719,488 at frame 2,000 and at the end (largest sample 230,748,160), framehash.bin equal to the original's capture byte for byte, the spilled recording equal to the in-memory one byte for byte (course_season). The split of the old 166 MB between the frame records (1,628 B per frame = 83 MB) and the recorder events was computed, not profiled.

[S7.8, kind `method`] host.cpp TerrainLogBound drops LiveTerrain's log lines through a const_cast on LiveTerrain::log(), the only access the class gives; the vector is LiveTerrain's own member, so the write is defined, but it reaches into S3's object. The S3 option in 8_merge.md section 3 (set_keep_log / calls) removes it.
path to resolution: S3 applies 8_merge.md section 3; the app then calls set_keep_log(false)
